args.title: checkout-api: rolled back v2.3.1 → v2.3.0 after failing health checks
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) after the latest deploy to v2.3.1. Observed error rate was 18% with healthy=false across all regions.

Action taken: rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt failed with a partial_failure orchestrator error after completing us-east only, leaving the fleet in a mixed state (us-east v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). The rollback was retried and completed successfully in all three production regions.

Current state: all regions on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate down to ~0.2%.

Note: v2.3.1 also appears in staging as v2.3.1-rc with status unhealthy, so the regression likely predates the production rollout — worth investigating before any redeploy of v2.3.1. Recommendation is to leave v2.3.0 in place and root-cause the v2.3.1 health-check failures.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did land — INC-0001 exists, so no retry was needed (the idempotency key would have prevented a duplicate anyway).

## Summary

**Incident:** checkout-api was failing health checks in all production regions on v2.3.1 (healthy=false, 18% error rate).

**Rollback target:** v2.3.0 — the most recent release with `status: healthy` in production. (v2.3.1-rc only ever existed in staging and is itself unhealthy; v2.2.9 was healthy but older than needed.)

**What happened:**
1. First `rollback` to v2.3.0 returned `partial_failure: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error`. Verification showed a mixed fleet — us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on the bad v2.3.1.
2. Retried the rollback; it completed cleanly in all three regions.
3. Verified: all regions on v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate down from 18% → 0.2%.

**Incident opened:** INC-0001, SEV2, documenting the rollback, the partial-failure/retry, and final state. It also flags that the v2.3.1 regression was already visible in staging (v2.3.1-rc unhealthy) — recommend root-causing before any redeploy.

One note on approval policy: the change-manager approval requirement applies to deploying a version that has *never* been healthy in production. v2.3.0 has a prior healthy production release, so this rollback was within normal runbook authority and did not need sign-off. If you'd like v2.3.1 re-released later, that will require change-manager approval plus a fix.
